findings.title: No regression fixture for sidecar-present-but-wrong-hash
findings.description: In release_audit_harness_runner_v1.py, sidecar_hash() returns None when the sidecar is absent OR when its content is not a valid 64-hex string. Only the absent-sidecar case produces BLOCKED; a present-but-wrong-hash sidecar correctly produces FAIL. However the runner self-test (self_test/make_zip) always writes a correct sidecar — there is no case where the sidecar holds an intentionally wrong hash. A regression that silently made sidecar_hash() return None for a wrong hash (e.g. by broadening the regex) would not be caught.
findings.recommended_action: Add a self-test case where the sidecar file contains an intentionally wrong (but validly formatted) SHA-256. Expected check decision: FAIL.

findings.title: Malformed sidecar silently becomes BLOCKED, not documented
findings.description: If the sidecar file exists but contains non-hex content (e.g. 'MISSING' or a corrupt string), sidecar_hash() returns None. The resulting check decision is BLOCKED (same as absent sidecar). This prevents a false FAIL but is undocumented and untested. A malformed sidecar that should signal tampering is indistinguishable from a legitimately absent sidecar.
findings.recommended_action: Distinguish 'sidecar absent' (BLOCKED) from 'sidecar malformed' (FAIL). Add fixture documenting current BLOCKED behavior.
findings.first_pass_action: Documented in fixture sidecar_regression_validator.py with expected BLOCKED decision.

findings.title: Missing edge-case fixtures for downloaded_sha256/download_sha256 normalization
findings.description: fixtures/landed_receipt_self_verify/ has three cases: legacy_download_sha256_PASS (only download_sha256 present), both_keys_differ_BLOCKED, mismatched_asset_BLOCKED. Missing: (a) canonical_only_PASS: receipt has only downloaded_sha256, no download_sha256 field — the canonical path. (b) neither_key_BLOCKED: receipt has neither field — should produce BLOCKED. These gaps leave the normalizer untested for its canonical and total-absence paths.
findings.recommended_action: Add canonical_only_PASS.json and neither_key_BLOCKED.json fixtures. Run landed_receipt_self_verify_v1.py against them in CI.
findings.first_pass_action: Fixtures added to repo at fixtures/landed_receipt_self_verify/ (canonical_only_PASS.json, neither_key_BLOCKED.json).

findings.title: landed_receipt_self_verify_v1.py returns exit code 2 for PASS_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFIRMED
findings.description: main() returns 0 only for PASS_PROVEN; it returns 2 for PASS_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFIRMED. PASS_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFIRMED is a valid non-error outcome (asset not local, hashes match in receipt). CI callers that check exit code would treat a key-confirmed receipt as an error, forcing downstream workflows to either ignore exit codes or paper over the exit code with || true.
findings.recommended_action: Return 0 for both PASS_PROVEN and PASS_RECEIPT_KEY_CONFIRMED. Return non-zero only for BLOCKED. Not fixing in first pass — requires OS-side code change.
findings.first_pass_action: Documented. Fixture neither_key_BLOCKED.json also covers the BLOCKED exit-code case.

findings.title: Partial decompressed file not deleted on zstd timeout
findings.description: In release_audit_harness_runner_v1.py, run_binary_to_file() opens the target file before starting subprocess.run(). On TimeoutExpired, the partial file may already have bytes written. materialize() sets the check to FAIL (correct) but the return expression `(target if target.exists() and target.stat().st_size > 0 else None)` can still return the partial file as zip_path. audit() then calls check_zip() on the corrupt partial file, producing misleading additional check rows in the output despite the upstream FAIL.
findings.recommended_action: In run_binary_to_file(), on TimeoutExpired, delete the partial target file before returning. In materialize(), guard zip_path return on returncode == 0. Not fixing in first pass — requires runner code change.

findings.title: Release audit harness runner cannot process tar.zst releases
findings.description: The new sticky release (MB-FULL-STICKY-RECEIPT-KEY-SELFVERIFY-20260601T2251Z) uses the .tar.zst format. The runner's materialize() function only handles .zip and .zip.zst, returning BLOCKED with 'expected .zip or .zip.zst' for any other extension. The GitHub workflow (metablooms-release-audit-harness.yml) would therefore return BLOCKED when triaged against this release. The REQUIRED member paths ({root}/scripts/mpp/mpp.sh etc.) are also ZIP-path-based and would not apply to a tar archive. The prior durable release (metablooms-stage12-reconciled-20260522T0058Z) correctly uses .zip.zst and remains auditable.
findings.recommended_action: Extend materialize() to handle .tar.zst; add tar-based required-member check. Alternatively, require future full-OS releases to use .zip.zst for harness compatibility. Not fixing in first pass — broad runner change.
findings.first_pass_action: Documented. A BLOCKED fixture expectation is recorded in sidecar_regression_validator.py.

findings.title: Workflow does not fail-fast on absent sidecar before passing to runner
findings.description: metablooms-release-audit-harness.yml downloads the release asset and sidecar, then passes artifact_path to the runner. If the .sha256 sidecar were absent from the release, gh release download would error on that asset but the workflow has no explicit pre-runner SHA check. The runner would then emit BLOCKED (not FAIL). This is acceptable but means a missing sidecar is treated as a blocker rather than a hard error at the workflow level.
findings.recommended_action: Optionally add a workflow-level sha256sum verification step before invoking the runner, so sidecar absence is a hard workflow error rather than a runner BLOCKED.

findings.title: New sticky release not in durability ledger — durable floor unchanged
findings.description: The sticky release (786fd1...) was published 2026-06-01T23:20Z. The durability ledger (DURABILITY_LEDGER_RECEIPT_KEY_NORMALIZED.json, created 2026-06-01T22:36Z) predates the release and contains no entry for it. The K2 floor (sha: 4efc7472..., binary_readback_real_hash_pass: true) is intact and is the current durable floor. The shrunk stage008B baseline (sha: 38fe0f2d...) is PENDING_PHONE_RELEASE_ASSET_READBACK. Per audit rule: binary readback proof is required before a new floor is declared. No action taken.
findings.recommended_action: After phone readback of the sticky release proves SHA match, add a durability ledger entry for 786fd1... with binary_readback_real_hash_pass: true. Do not replace K2 floor until a stronger binary readback proves a newer candidate.

findings.title: Release audit harness self-test missing sidecar-mismatch and tar.zst cases
findings.description: The runner's self_test() exercises three cases: positive (PASS), missing_mpp (FAIL), traversal (FAIL). Missing: (1) sidecar present with wrong hash → expect FAIL on artifact_sha_sidecar. (2) sidecar file contains non-hex content → expect BLOCKED on artifact_sha_sidecar. (3) artifact is .tar.zst (unsupported) → expect BLOCKED on artifact_extension. Adding these to the runner's make_zip/cases list would catch future regressions.
findings.recommended_action: Extend make_zip() to accept a wrong_sidecar_hash=False and malformed_sidecar=False param; add cases to self_test() cases list. Not changing runner in first pass.
findings.first_pass_action: Standalone validator fixtures/release_audit_harness/sidecar_regression_validator.py covers these cases without modifying the runner.
